<div class="research-page"><p class="eyebrow">SELECTED WORK &amp; RESEARCH COMMUNICATION</p><h1>Research portfolio</h1><p class="intro-lede">A curated look at real research questions, datasets, and analytical approaches. This page replaces the earlier illustrative sample charts with descriptions grounded in completed or ongoing projects.</p>
<section class="research-section" id="forest"><span class="project-type">REMOTE SENSING &amp; SPATIAL DATA</span><h2>01 / Colorado Front Range forest change</h2><p><strong>Data:</strong> NLCD land-cover maps for 2001 and 2021, burned-area datasets, and elevation models.</p><p><strong>Analysis:</strong> land-cover transitions, forest-type change, spatial overlap with burned areas, and elevation-related patterns using Python and Google Earth Engine.</p><div class="result-inline"><strong>~19%</strong><span>decrease in mapped forest cover in the team’s 2001–2021 study; an association, not a causal estimate</span></div><p class="quiet">Collaborative work through ESIIL. The presentation includes team and mentor contributions. Research figures and slide files are not republished here pending sharing review.</p><a href="projects.html#esiil">Read the project summary</a></section>
<section class="research-section" id="soil"><span class="project-type">ENVIRONMENTAL–ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT</span><h2>02 / Synthetic humic substances for agricultural applications</h2><p><strong>System:</strong> four crop-residue-derived production pathways and modeled applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple systems in China.</p><p><strong>Assessment:</strong> life cycle impacts, internal production costs, monetized environmental externalities, crop-specific substitution scenarios, and regional electricity mixes.</p><p><strong>Interpretation:</strong> results depend on pathway assumptions, crop conditions, data sources, and system boundaries. Modeled economic impacts are not direct measurements of farm profitability.</p><p class="quiet">Research presented in Chinese at the 2025 Chinese Ecological Congress. An English summary is provided here; complete unpublished slides and underlying tables are not public.</p><a href="projects.html#shs">Read the project summary</a></section>
<section class="research-section" id="grazing"><span class="project-type">MODEL WORKFLOWS &amp; SCENARIO TESTING</span><h2>03 / Grazing-management scenarios</h2><p><strong>Tools:</strong> MEMS Grazing Scheduler and related model workflows, with DayCent experience from training and project work.</p><p><strong>Tasks:</strong> management scenario input preparation, run testing, output interpretation, reproducible documentation, and carbon-accounting requirement review.</p><p><strong>Scope:</strong> these were ecosystem modeling and accounting tasks, not an independently developed ranch-profitability model.</p><p class="quiet">Only general work descriptions are shared; private project repositories and model input files remain restricted.</p><a href="projects.html#landengine">Read the project summary</a></section>
